title: Cast rate to float when constructing Poisson to ensure consistent log prob behavior
author: dylanhmorris

comments.author: Qazalbash
comments.body: Hi @dylanhmorris, I have proposed a fix. Please see #2182.

comments.author: Qazalbash
comments.body:
Interesting behaviour when validation is on!

```python
In [1]: import numpyro.distributions as dist

In [2]: int_rate = dist.Poisson(2, validate_args=True)

In [3]: float_rate = dist.Poisson(2., validate_args=True)

In [4]: int_rate.log_prob(2)
Out[4]: Array(-1.306853, dtype=float32)

In [5]: float_rate.log_prob(2)
Out[5]: Array(-1.306853, dtype=float32)

In [6]: int_rate.log_prob(1.999999)
<ipython-input-6-37287a8a65a9>:1: UserWarning: Out-of-support values provided to log prob method. The value argument should be within the support.
  int_rate.log_prob(1.999999)
Out[6]: Array(-inf, dtype=float32)

In [7]: float_rate.log_prob(1.999999)
<ipython-input-7-119894d57215>:1: UserWarning: Out-of-support values provided to log prob method. The value argument should be within the support.
  float_rate.log_prob(1.999999)
Out[7]: Array(-inf, dtype=float32)
```

@dylanhmorris, we can avoid the issue by enabling the validation 😄.

comments.author: dylanhmorris
comments.body: Good point! I still think it's worth changing the behavior to ensure things work more predictably with `validate_args=False`, but I defer to others.

comments.author: tillahoffmann
comments.body:
This is an interesting one. I agree that we should probably cast to the appropriate dtype for the constraint of the parameter because the behavior can be surprising. E.g., passing an int covariance matrix to a multivariate normal leaves the passed parameter as int, but the Cholesky decomposition has floating dtype.

```python
In [1]: from numpyro import distributions as dists
        from jax import numpy as jnp

In [2]: def get_args(dist):
   ...:     return {key: getattr(dist, key, None) for key in dist.arg_constraints}
   ...: 

In [10]: get_args(dists.MultivariateNormal(0, jnp.ones((1, 1), dtype=int)))
Out[10]: 
{'loc': array([0]),
 'covariance_matrix': Array([[1]], dtype=int32),
 'precision_matrix': Array([[1.]], dtype=float32),
 'scale_tril': Array([[1.]], dtype=float32)}
```

Likewise, if we pass the precision matrix as int, it stays as int, but the cov matrix is float.

```python
In [11]: get_args(dists.MultivariateNormal(0, precision_matrix=jnp.ones((1, 1), dtype=int)))
Out[11]: 
{'loc': array([0]),
 'covariance_matrix': Array([[1.]], dtype=float32),
 'precision_matrix': Array([[1]], dtype=int32),
 'scale_tril': Array([[1.]], dtype=float32)}
```

I think we can derive the dtype unambiguously from the constraint?
